problem: The three jobs arrive as a row of small icon cards under the S05 world, and nothing on the inn itself changes: the free link never goes live on the inn, no rate tags appear at site and inn, the book never reaches the desk. On W001701 Findable draw a solid line from a small search mark to a door-page on the inn facade; on W001708 Bookable put two equal blank rate tags, one on the site and one on that door-page, with '='; on W001716 Remembered set the guest book on the inn's desk with the thank-you note and leaf beside it; W001732 consent box sits on the book. Reduce the card row to three small labels beside those objects, or remove it.

problem: After the world clears, 23 s play as a left cluster plus six generic inns that have no line to the practice; each inn's 'own ceiling' and blank tag are too small to read at 720p, and the room-count axis with an unlabelled dashed marker explains nothing.

Scale the inns and their ceiling line plus blank tag about 2x so the tag under each line is legible. Remove the room-count axis and its marker (S18 introduces the axis with words that support it).

problem: Credential, handwritten note, newsletter and a very small guest float in four corners of an empty page with no shared ground, so the comparison 'a note an innkeeper would be proud of versus a newsletter with a name tag' is not staged as a comparison.

Keep the You/Owner table beat on W001878.

problem: The detached drip-campaign envelope chain sits inside the same outlined panel as the signed guest book, a few pixels to its right, so it reads as what the book leads to rather than what the guest did not sign up for.

problem: F07 frames the innkeeper from the chin down: a known character appears headless for 3.7 s, the only person in a 190 s stretch, and the planned 'card and pen slide into view' never happens.

problem: The seasonal-note card (and the S20 October note) is a leaf with a dashed line climbing bottom-left to top-right; at 720p it reads as a small rising chart, placed in the same frame as the 'Direct share of bookings' report. The plan prohibits a rising line in S15.

problem: The end state carries about 15 text blocks, and a long curve runs from the law labels to the innkeeper's head, so 'not legal advice' appears to be something she says or holds.
fix: Remove the curve. When 'Inside the rules' lands on W002334, fade the 'after checkout' cards to 30 percent. Set the law labels as a short list directly under the boundary and relay field.

problem: The two channel boxes attach by short dashed tails to the Owner's head, reading as speech bubbles (the owner saying 'Innkeeper associations'), not as unproven routes toward the practice.

problem: The kicker 'IF' is small grey caps; the full-size sentence 'Agencies already retain 30-room inns at $1,500 a month and owners prefer it' reads as a stated fact for about 10 s, against C011 (must not imply agencies serve the band) and C027. From 887 to 897 the only other object is a phone in the bottom-left corner.

problem: The heading and band sit on an otherwise empty page for 9 s (904-913); the busiest frame then holds about 30 text items (five rail tags, six $800 tags, six '8 h', five ledger lines, two columns) with the bottom third empty. Legible at full size, but two to three times the density of the accepted EP007 R60-R63 cards: it reads as a spreadsheet.
fix: Fade each rail tag to 30 percent once its number is used and remove '$1,000 or $1,250' after W002557; replace the six '8 h' labels with the single note; when line 4 lands collapse ledger lines 1-3 to 30 percent; move the whole layout down 60 px so the columns use the lower third. Start the rail on W002532 as now but let the six inns draw on W002523 'modeled' so the opening is not empty.

problem: The observed AHLA count sits under the persistent 'MODELED SCENARIO' band, so a sourced population can read as part of the model.

problem: The room-count axis puts numeric ticks at 20 and 40 and draws the window edges at about 24 and 37 rooms, with 'too small' over the 20 tick and the agency figures from 40. It states band edges the narration says nobody knows, implies the episode's own 20-room inn is too small, and places agencies at the top of the 20 to 40 band (C011, C015 boundaries).
fix: Remove the 20 and 40 tick labels in seg061; keep two dashed edges with '?' and 'width unknown'; put the agency figures beyond the right edge without numbers. Add numbers only when W002926 'Forty to eighty' extends the axis, labelling just 40 and 80 on the extension.

problem: By 1060 the frame holds three full slots, a stop/move-up row and the axis, about 28 labels, all at equal weight, so the eye has no current point.
fix: Dim slot 1 to 40 percent on W002860 'Renewal', dim slot 2 on W002887 'And access', and dim all three slots when the fork appears on W002903; drop the small 'first slow month' label.

problem: For 36 s every object is packed small into the left 40 percent of the frame while the right 60 percent is empty; the screen also shows 'PMS partner managers', an acronym never spoken (S16's build removed it for that reason).

problem: F08 to F09 is a near-same-setup jump: the camera shifts, the door and key rack move, and the guest pops from writing at the card to back-turned at the book. See also s20-1132.417-f08-last.png.
